about.title: Dunsmuir Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: In a place the size of Dunsmuir, a death is never anonymous. Roughly 1,582 people live here, so a loss tied to I-5, Dunsmuir Avenue or Castle Avenue is felt at the post office, the school and the diner within days. Public records show the city closed 2025 with no traffic deaths, and that matters. Still, wrongful death claims reach beyond the highway. A fatal fall at a rental property, a medication error, an unguarded worksite, or a collision on the I-5 southbound lanes all raise one legal question: did someone else's carelessness end a life? California allows certain surviving family members to bring a civil claim, entirely separate from anything a prosecutor may or may not do. We handle wrongful death matters in Siskiyou County. Tell us what happened, and our team will review the facts, explain who has standing, and work on contingency if the case moves forward.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, with a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We sort this out early so the right people are protected.

items.title: The two-year clock, watched closely
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting started sooner keeps options open.

items.title: Every loss accounted for
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance are all recoverable under California law. We build the claim around your family's real losses, not a formula.

items.question: My family member was killed on I-5 near Dunsmuir. Does it matter that we live somewhere else?
items.answer: Not for your right to bring a claim. Wrongful death cases arising from a crash in Siskiyou County can generally be filed here regardless of where the family lives. We can explain venue and handle the local logistics so you don't have to travel back and forth.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from any criminal case. Waiting for a criminal outcome can actually eat into the two-year filing deadline, so it's worth speaking with us now.

items.question: Do you charge us anything?
items.answer: No. We work on contingency, which means no fee unless there is a recovery.
